concept.title: Who can see your tree
concept.shortdesc: Your tree is yours: you decide who gets a copy, and your PC keeps it safe.

conbody.p: Your tree is yours. does not send it anywhere. Nobody who makes can see it.
You decide what goes in your tree, where you keep it and who gets a copy. That makes you the data controller for the people in it. This includes any who are still alive.

section.title: Copies that your PC makes
section.p: Some PCs keep the Documents folder in OneDrive. If yours does, your trees go to OneDrive with the rest of that folder. OneDrive keeps them under your own account. says which folder your trees are in.
To see whether Documents goes to OneDrive, open the OneDrive settings and choose Sync and back up.
File History can also copy your folders to another drive. To find it, search for File History in the Start menu.
Your PC and OneDrive make these copies, not . Nobody who makes can see them.

section.title: Copies that you save
section.p: A copy that you save goes where you choose. shows how. A folder that is kept in step with a service, such as Dropbox or Google Drive, sends that service a copy too. It keeps it under your account.

section.title: Your files are not locked by
section.p: does not encrypt your trees. They are ordinary files. What keeps them safe is your PC.
BitLocker, or device encryption on some PCs, encrypts your drive. To see whether it is on, open Settings and search for encryption. Keep a password or a PIN on your Windows account too.
If you give someone a copy of a tree, they can read all of it.

section.title: Pictures from a website
section.p: A tree can point to a picture on a website. says what that website can see, and where the picture is kept.
